name: Toy Bricks
summary: A toy-box world of glossy plastic bricks: stud-covered baseplates, tiled roads, transparent-blue water plates and a little toy figure.
description: Everything is built from interlocking plastic parts seen from a steep 3/4 front view: bricks, plates, smooth tiles and round bricks, each baked to sprites at startup by a small cell renderer that gives every part a glossy front gradient, a sheen band, lit rims, dark gaps to its neighbours and a round stud with a highlight crescent on every open top. The ground is a green baseplate covered in studs, with raised lime and grey plates, smooth grey road tiles with white lane dashes and transparent-blue water plates. The main character is a molded toy figure with a yellow cylinder head, printed face and claw hands, posed like a played-with toy: rigid legs swing on the hip pin, arms on the shoulder pins, the head looks around, the helmet pops up when it is hit. Creatures are brick beetles in two designs, a translucent ghost piece and a brick-built robot; they click together from the baseplate and pop apart into bricks. Saturated toy-box primaries, crisp and cheerful.

difficulty.why: Props and creatures are cell grids described with a few part() calls, and the renderer adds gloss, gaps, studs and shadows automatically. The molded figures are hand-written canvas paths with several gradients, prints and per-frame poses, and round parts need their own cylinder slices, so new characters take more care than new props.

technique.renderer: Canvas 2D (procedural, no image assets) with a small brick-cell renderer and vector figure painter that bake sprites at init
technique.resolution: Native resolution. Sprites are baked at K = clamp(round(screenH/360 × 1.6 × 2)/2, 2.5, 7) px per world unit (about 1.6× the screen scale, so element sheets and close-ups stay crisp) and drawn down-scaled; blits snap to whole screen pixels. Ground chunks (256 units) are drawn at up to 2.5 px per unit.
technique.summary: A model is a grid of cells (x right, y toward the viewer, z up; 1 cell = 1 stud × 1 stud × 1 plate) where every cell stores the id of the part it belongs to. Seen straight from the front with no yaw, only top and front faces exist, so every face is an axis-aligned rectangle: rows are drawn back to front, plates bottom to top, and the part ids tell the renderer where to put rims, gaps and studs.
technique.linework: No outlines. Forms are separated by 1-px-per-0.28-unit lines from the part structure: a white rim (alpha 0.6) along the top edge of every front face, a dark gap line (black, alpha 0.4) where a part sits on another part, dark vertical gaps (alpha 0.36) between neighbouring parts, a light left end (alpha 0.3) and a darker right end (alpha 0.2). Prints (faces, windows, arrows) are flat #1b1d22 shapes.
technique.shading: Front faces: vertical gradient over the whole part, colour ×1.2+12 at the top edge, ×1.02 at 13%, ×0.88 at 60%, ×0.70 at the bottom, plus a horizontal sheen band (white 0.24 alpha at 10% of the part width, fading to a 0.12 black at the right end). Top faces: flat colour ×1.06+4 with a white back rim. Round parts: horizontal cylinder gradient ×0.95 / ×1.2 highlight at 20% / ×1.02 / ×0.8 / ×0.62.
technique.lighting: Bright studio light from the upper left: highlights on the left and top edges, cast shadows sheared to the lower right by (0.36, 0.2) units per unit of height and blurred (0.9 K px), drawn at 0.42–0.5 alpha in a cool rgba(10,25,45). Only transparent emissive parts (lamp heads, robot eyes, orbiting beacons) get an additive radial glow. A soft cool vignette and a warm-white light spot in the top-left corner finish the frame.
technique.texture: None. The texture is the studs themselves: a stud on every open top cell of every part and on every baseplate cell, each a baked sprite with a cylinder gradient, a lighter top, an 0.34-unit white highlight crescent on its upper left and a soft contact shadow to the lower right.

paletteRules: Only saturated toy-box primaries plus white, black, tan and two greys; every colour is a flat plastic colour, never a texture or a noise mix.
Shading comes only from the fixed gloss recipe (×1.2 rim to ×0.7 bottom) — never pick a second, hand-darkened shade for the same part.
Transparent parts (water, lamp heads, beacons, ghost, debris of the ghost) keep their colour at 0.5–0.88 alpha and get brighter highlights; only transparent warm parts glow.
The world is green/tan/grey/blue; creatures are red, white, blue and clear; the main character is orange, yellow and dark blue so it pops on every ground.
Prints are always #1b1d22 flat shapes with tiny white glints, like pad-printed toy parts.
UI uses the same part colours (white, yellow, blue bricks, black tiles) with #1b1d22 as the booklet line colour.

world.summary: An endless stud-covered baseplate drawn row by row into cached 256-unit chunks. One cell = one stud (6 units across, 4.2 units deep). Every cell has a material and a level (-1 water, 0 baseplate, +1 raised plates); a raised cell is drawn 2.1 units higher and shows its glossy front edge when the cell in front of it is lower, so the ground reads as real plates stacked on a baseplate.
layers: Base: per-cell top colour (baseplate #47a347, dark green #2f8540, raised lime #8cc63f, tan #e2cb96, raised grey #a7acb0, road #666d73, curb #c6cbce, water #3d92e8 / #2b70d2)
Plate seams: dark 0.2-alpha lines every 16 studs on baseplates, every 4 on raised plates, every 2 on road tiles (plus a 0.16 white top line per tile row)

Edges: white rim on the back and left edge of raised cells, 2.2-unit contact-shadow gradient below and 2.4-unit shadow right of higher neighbours, a glossy 2.1-unit front face (×1.16+10 → ×0.84 → ×0.64) on cells above a lower neighbour
Roads: winding constant-width bands from |noise| / |gradient| < 11.5 units, curb tiles where a road cell touches a non-road cell, white lane-dash tiles on the centre line in a 2-on / 2-off pattern
Studs: one baked stud sprite per cell centre (transparent pale-blue studs on water); none on roads and curbs

Toy parts instead of a stud, grown in beds: flower plates (5 petals around a yellow centre) only inside flower beds (noise/70 > 0.68, 30 % of the cells there), one colour per bed from a 160-unit noise field with rare accents; leaf plants in clumps (noise/48 > 0.64, 14 %), 0.4 % elsewhere; loose round plates 0.08 %; lily pads on open water (2 %)
Per frame: white cross-shaped glints blinking on 12% of the water cells

characters.summary: Two construction methods share one light. The main character and the translucent ghost are molded toy figures painted with canvas paths (gradients, rims, prints) and baked per frame and facing; the brick beetle and the robot are cell grids built from bricks, plates and round bricks with printed faces, baked per frame and mirrored per facing by mirroring the grid (so the light stays on the left).
rules: Main character: a toy figure ~31 units tall and ~15 wide — blue legs on a hip piece, an orange trapezoid torso with printed strap, belt and red bandana, sloping arms ending in yellow C-shaped claw hands, a yellow cylinder head with a printed face, a tan pith helmet with a brown band and a brown backpack on the side away from the facing direction.

It is posed like a real toy: legs are rigid pieces rotating on the hip pin (±0.42 rad), arms rotate on the shoulder pins, hands turn on the wrist pin, the head print looks around (face offset −0.3 … 1.6 units), the helmet is a separate piece that lags the hop and pops up 2.2 units on a hit. 16 poses per facing: 8 walk, 4 idle fidgets, blink, dash crouch, dash lunge, hurt (eyes wide, O-mouth).

Small creature, two designed variants picked by the actor's seed: a red brick beetle (2×3 red brick with a printed grin, dark red shell plate, two white round eye bricks) or a yellow striped beetle (black stripe print, black shell, one tall and one short eye, a black round antenna with a red tip). 6 scuttle poses — feet jump one stud, the body hops one plate, the eyes lag the hop — plus a hit pose (jumps a plate, feet splayed, X-printed eyes).

Fast creature: a translucent ghost piece (~20 units wide): a sheet with raised arms and a wavy hem, cool clear fill, a white rim, a white gloss arc and printed eyes and O-mouth; 6 poses (arms alternate, hem ripples) + a hit pose (flared, arms high, eyes 1.35× wider); hovers on an eased 2.4 s bob with a faint blue glow.

Large creature: a brick robot (7×3×22 cells, ~42 units wide): grey feet, black hip plate, blue torso with a printed grille and chest panel, grey arms with yellow shoulder plates and red hands, a grey head with glowing red eyes, a black antenna with a transparent red tip. 6 stomp poses (one foot lifts a plate, arms swing a stud, head and antenna lag one pose) + a hit pose (arms raised five plates, antenna glow larger).
No outlines; parts are separated by the renderer's rims and gaps. Every figure casts a soft shadow to the lower right.

props.summary: Scenery is brick-built on the same stud grid as the ground: props snap to whole studs, sit on the plate they stand on (raised plates lift them by 2.1 units) and are y-sorted with the figures. Each prop is one cell grid baked once with its own sheared, blurred shadow.
rules: Trees (5×3×15): a 1×1 round brown trunk of two round bricks, a dark green 3×3 plate, two stepped crown layers of green and bright green bricks, a lime top plate and red or yellow 1×1 round fruit plates on the steps.
Pines (5×3×16): a short round trunk and alternating dark green bricks and green plates stepping in from 5 to 3 to 1 stud.

Small props: a green bush brick with round leaf and flower plates, a stepped grey rock pile, a white fence (two posts, two smooth rails), a pile of loose coloured bricks, a sign post (round brown post + white tile with a printed red arrow), an orange cone with a white stripe, a black lamp post with a glowing transparent yellow head.

A small house (5×4×14): red walls laid in running bond (staggered 2/3-stud bricks), a printed blue door, two white window parts with printed blue glass and white mullions, a white plate, a dark grey roof brick and a dark red chimney.
Props only stand where every footprint cell has the same material and never on plate edges, roads or water; lamps and cones may stand on curbs.
Tall props (trees, pines, lamps, house) fade to 0.32 alpha when the main character is behind them, and the figure is redrawn over them at 0.72 alpha.

effects.name: Plastic pop
effects.how: The core flash of every hit, burst, pickup and celebration: a white 4-point star (cool blue for clear pieces) that snaps open from 45 % to full size with outQuad and a thin white ring around it, 0.12–0.22 s.

effects.name: Flying single bricks
effects.how: Bursts throw baked loose parts (1×1 brick, 1×2 brick, 2×2 plate, 1×1 round plate, 1×1 plate) in the colours of what burst; they tumble (±7 rad/s), fly with vz 50–150, gravity 330, drag 1.3, bounce, leave a soft shadow near the ground and fade in the last 25 %. Ghost pieces float upward.

effects.name: Loose studs (residue)
effects.how: Each burst also drops 3–5 round 1×1 plates that barely jump (vz 25–30) and lie on the baseplate for 1.8–2.2 s before fading – what is left of the creature.

effects.name: Stud ring
effects.how: An ellipse (r × 0.8 r) easing out to 22–56 units, white stroke at 0.8·k alpha, with 4–16 yellow studs riding on it; the celebration ring's studs advance in quarter steps.

effects.name: Click-together appearance
effects.how: Brick creatures are built up from the baseplate in whole plate rows (outQuad over 75 % of 0.45 s) while two loose bricks drop in, then they press down (squash 0.92) and spring back (1.04) with a white pop on top – the click. The ghost fades in, drops 10 units onto its peg and un-stretches.

effects.name: Pop apart
effects.how: A vanishing creature swells (1.08 × 1.05) and whites out for 14 %, then its hit pose splits into brick-sized blocks (2×3, robot 3×5) that jump out and up, land on the baseplate and fade; positions advance on twos and rotations snap to 30° steps (stop-motion). The ghost piece floats apart and shrinks. At most 8 per frame.

effects.name: Stud coins
effects.how: Collectibles are round stud coins spinning through 10 baked frames: azure #2f9bff small, gold #ffc81e large with a gold glow; raised ring, highlight crescent, edge band, hovering 4.4–6 units with a twinkle star.

effects.name: Projectile and orbiting beacon
effects.how: A yellow 1×1 round plate with two fading copies and a pale yellow speed line; a transparent orange round brick on a black plate with a yellow cap hovering 10 ± 1.4 units in a warm glow.

atmosphere.summary: Clean toy photography: one bright studio light from the upper left baked into every gradient, rim and stud crescent, cool soft shadows, almost no colour grading. Only transparent warm parts glow.
rules: Cast shadows of props and brick creatures: every column's footprint sheared (0.36, 0.2) units per unit of height to the lower right, filled black, blurred 0.9 K px, alpha 0.42–0.5.
Figures without a grid (main character, ghost, collectibles, beacons, debris) get a soft radial ellipse shadow rgba(10,25,45,0.5 → 0) offset 1.6 units to the right.
Glow sprites: 64 px radial gradients (0.9 → 0.32 → 0 alpha) in warm rgb(255,210,110), red rgb(255,70,40), cool rgb(120,190,255) or gold, drawn additively — only on emissive transparent parts.
Screen overlay: radial vignette from rgba(20,40,80,0) at 0.36 h to rgba(14,26,60,0.34) at the corners, plus a warm-white light spot rgba(255,252,235,0.16) at the top-left corner.
Ground light: only blinking white glints on transparent water plates.
Overlay screens tint the world with a pale booklet blue: radial-gradient(rgba(232,245,253,.42), rgba(120,176,224,.52)).
No grain, no blur, no bloom pass, no outlines; the gloss recipe carries all the light.

ui.summary: Brick-built HUD and instruction-booklet cards. Panels are bricks: a glossy vertical gradient, inset white top/left rims and dark bottom/right rims, a 4 px hard drop edge in a darker shade, and a row of side-view studs (CSS gradients) sitting on the top edge. Bars are dark recessed tiles whose fill is a plate seen from above, covered in studs. Cards are booklet pages: white with a pale blue bottom, a 3 px #1b1d22 border and hard 6 px drop edge, a big Titan One step number in the corner and a parts-callout box around the icon with a small '1x' count.

motion: The toy is animated like a brickfilm: poses are held and stepped, not tweened. Main character walk: 8 poses at frame = floor(anim·1.3) mod 8 (~12 fps at walking speed): legs ±0.42 / ±0.28 / 0 rad on the hip pins, arms counter-swing at 1.25× the leg angle, the figure hops 1.2 units at passing, the helmet lags the hop.
Idle: 4 fidget poses held 0.75 s each (look further toward the facing side, look away while turning a hand on its wrist pin, small breath), and a blink pose for 0.16 s every 3.8 s.

Dash: crouch pose for the first 50 ms (body 1.4 lower, leaning back, arms back = anticipation), then the lunge (leaning 0.22 rad, legs ±0.7, arms back) with two white copies two units apart; hurt pose while hurtT > 0.62 with a red tint; invulnerability blinks at 18 Hz.
Beetles: 6 poses at anim·2.7, robot 6 poses at anim·1.8, ghost 6 poses at 7 fps + seed with an eased hover (holds at the top and bottom, own phase per actor) – crowds never move in lock-step.
Hit: hit pose + white flash while flash > 0.25, knocked 2 units in the push direction for the first half, squash 1.06 × 0.95.
All brick motion is in whole cells (studs, plates); debris and coins move smoothly, break-up blocks move on twos.
Coins spin 1.4 sets per second and bob ±0.9 units; floating numbers pop from 0.6 to 1.15 in the first 14 % of their life.
do: Build every prop, creature, icon and debris piece from real part sizes on one grid: 1 stud = 6 units across, 4.2 deep, 1 plate = 2.1 units, 1 brick = 3 plates.
Let the part structure do the line work: rims on top edges, dark gaps between parts, staggered bricks in walls.
Put a stud on every open top that is not a smooth tile, and on every baseplate cell.
Use only flat saturated toy colours and the fixed gloss recipe; make transparent parts translucent with brighter highlights.
Snap props to whole studs so they sit exactly on the baseplate grid.
Mirror brick grids (not sprites) for the other facing so the light stays on the upper left.
Use smooth tiles (no studs) for roads, signs and roofs to give the eye calm areas.
Pose the figure like a toy: rotate rigid parts on their pins, hold poses, hop at passing; give every state its pose (blink, crouch, lunge, hurt).
Grow decorations in beds: one flower colour per bed, leaf plants in clumps, almost no loose studs elsewhere.
dont: Don't add outlines or strokes around parts.
Don't use noise, texture, dithering or per-cell colour jitter — plastic is clean and uniform.
Don't rotate the camera or show side faces; the look depends on the straight front 3/4 view.
Don't use half-stud offsets or arbitrary sizes; nothing may float between studs.
Don't use muted, earthy or pastel palettes for the world; it must feel like a toy box.
Don't make every surface studded: roads, curbs, signs and roof tiles stay smooth.
Don't use brand names, logos or embossed lettering on studs.
Don't tween poses smoothly or squash the figure – toys don't bend.
Don't sprinkle flowers and loose studs evenly over the baseplate.
performance: All parts are baked once in init(): the figure (16 poses × 2 facings), the ghost (7 poses + flipped copies), two beetle designs and the robot (7 poses × 2 mirrored grids each), 11 props with shadows, ~80 debris sprites and 20 coin frames. Per frame every object is 1–3 drawImage calls of cached canvases; pop-apart uses source rectangles (no clip paths) and is capped at 8 per frame; particles use one setTransform per brick. Ground chunks are drawn row by row as a generator (~25 ms per chunk spread over frames). Measured against the previous version in the same session: median frame +6 %, chunk build −9 %.
